'''''Heuchera sanguinea''''', called '''coral bells''', is a species of flowering plant in the genus ''[[Heuchera]]'', native to the US states of Arizona and New Mexico, and to northern Mexico.<ref name="791403-1" >{{cite web |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:791403-1 |title=''Heuchera sanguinea'' Engelm. |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2017 |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=Board of Trustees of the Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=25 January 2021 }}</ref> A number of cultivars are commercially available.<ref>{{cite web |title=''Heuchera sanguinea'' coral bells |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/8719/i-Heuchera-sanguinea-i/Details |publisher=The Royal Horticultural Society |accessdate=25 January 2021 |quote=Other common names; … crimson bells, fairy flower }}</ref> The Latin specific epithet ''sanguinea'' means blood-red, in reference to the color of the flowers.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Heuchera sanguinea (Alumroot, Coral Bells, Heuchera) {{!}} North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox|url=https://plants.ces.ncsu.edu/plants/heuchera-sanguinea/|access-date=2021-12-26|website=plants.ces.ncsu.edu}}</ref> Flowers are deep pink to red, sweetly fragrant, and bell-shaped. ''Heuchera sanguinea'' is a perennial herb.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Heuchera sanguinea - Plant Finder|url=https://www.missouribotanicalgarden.org/PlantFinder/PlantFinderDetails.aspx?kempercode=d250|access-date=2021-12-26|website=www.missouribotanicalgarden.org}}</ref> The plant attracts bees and hummingbirds.<ref name=":0" />
